plates.head: A swarm of AI agents that runs businesses on its own.
lines: New or existing, in any industry. Describe the business. The swarm sets itself up and runs it, day and night.
Ben Palaskas, founder · Seed round, November 2026

plates.head: Every business will run on AI agents. Almost none of them can set agents up.
lines: Running agents is a job of its own. Pick the models. Build the infrastructure. Write the policies. Connect them to the business's software. Manage them every day.
And it changes every week. New models, new tools, new best practice. Owners have no time to keep up, and no one on staff who can.
So they keep paying for the old way: a stack of SaaS subscriptions, people to operate it, or a chatbot that cannot do the job.

plates.head: Describe your business. Meet the team that runs it.
lines: One sentence in. About 90 seconds later: a team of agents shaped to that business, each with its own job, inside the tools it already uses, working day and night.
To the owner it is custom software built for them.

plates.head: A whole company's worth of work. No hiring, no building, no learning AI.
lines: No AI knowledge needed. AMTECH picks the models, builds the infrastructure, sets the policies and keeps up with the field.
Ready in minutes. No set-up project, no consultant, no code, no prompts to write.
Connects to any software. It sets up its own accounts and connections inside the tools the business already uses.
Improves itself. The team learns from its own work and gets better every week without anyone touching it.
Costs less than what it replaces. One price instead of a stack of subscriptions and the hours it takes to run them.

plates.head: Self-serve went public this week. AMTECH already runs ten businesses.
lines: A yard-care company: Its AI team built the website, takes bookings and answers customers. AMTECH is paid 8% of its revenue.
An e-commerce group: Eight stores, each run by its own team, under one main agent.
A lead-generation business: Moved its work to AMTECH after a Grok Bot agent could not do the job.
All of it before any public launch, sold directly by the founder. As of this week anyone can describe a business on amtechai.com and have a working team in under two minutes.

plates.head: Not one assistant. Hundreds of agents, working together.
lines: Twenty online stores, each with its own team for products, ads, email and customers, all under one main agent.
Every company in a private equity roll-up, each run by its own team, with one view across the portfolio.
One person can now run what used to take a whole company. Add a business, add a team. No hiring, ever.

plates.head: The fastest agents of any AI tool, on open-source models.
lines: Highest tokens per second of all competing AI tools. Agents finish work while others are still thinking.
Open-source models: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM-5.3. No lock-in to one lab, and the cost of running a team is cents, not dollars.
Sets up its own everything: its computer, its tools, its connections, its routines.
Built on what the best agent teams already use, so every advance in the field reaches our customers the same week.

plates.head: A new SaaS launches for some industry. Twenty minutes later, AMTECH has a better one, run by agents.
lines: Our research agents read what an industry says about itself online: forums, social media, market data. AMTECH turns that into a configuration. No code, no new team.

plates.head: What used to take a few million dollars and a separate team for every type of software takes AMTECH about 90 seconds.
lines: We use configurations of AMTECH, written in plain language, to break into entirely new industries. Each one is sold as its own product. The buyer does not need to know or want AI.
We can change our go-to-market faster than AI itself is changing.

plates.head: Private equity is buying service businesses to run them with AI.
lines: The money is already moving. Thrive Holdings raised over $2B to buy companies and run them with AI. General Catalyst set aside $1.5B for the same idea.
Every firm has to build that AI itself, company by company. AMTECH gives a whole portfolio a swarm on the day of the deal.
The trades are getting more competitive. Independent owners now go up against PE-backed rivals. AMTECH gives them the same leverage without selling.
It is the biggest change in how service businesses are owned and run in a generation, and AMTECH is the software it runs on.

plates.head: More people are starting businesses than ever, and more of them start online.
lines: AI made starting easy. One person can open a store, an agency or a content business in a weekend.
Running it is still hard. Marketing, customers, orders and books. These businesses have little or no staff and pay for a long list of SaaS tools instead.
That is the work an AMTECH swarm does from the first day, for a new business or an existing one.
AMTECH starts businesses of its own the same way, and keeps all of the revenue.

plates.head: Software margins on work businesses used to pay people for.
lines: Any business: starts at $50 a month and grows with use. Custom set-ups from $1,200 a month.
Agencies: one account, a team for every client. One sale brings dozens of businesses.
Operators and private equity: a team for every company in the portfolio, and 8% of each company's revenue.
AMTECH's own businesses: started and run by our own swarms. We keep all of the revenue.
Cost to run a team is cents a day, because the models are open-source and fast.

plates.head: The next trillion-dollar company will sell the work, not the tool.
lines: 36 million US businesses, and almost none of their work has been touched by software that does it for them.

Investors already pay billions for single pieces. Avoca is worth $1B for answering phones in the trades. Polsia raised at $250M five months in, with one founder. AMTECH runs the whole business, in every industry.
A billion-dollar company needs one in a thousand of them. Agencies and portfolios bring them in by the dozen.

plates.head: Everyone else sells a piece. AMTECH runs the whole business.
lines: Assistants like ChatGPT and Grok help one person, who still has to drive.
Agent builders like Lindy make you build and maintain every agent yourself.
Vertical SaaS like ServiceTitan sells one industry a tool, and still needs staff to run it.
AI roll-ups like Thrive have to buy a business before they can run it. They are customers, not rivals.

plates.head: Swarms of AI agents running businesses on their own, in every industry.
lines: Within a decade most businesses will be run by agents. AMTECH intends to be the one running them: new businesses and existing ones, in any industry our agents can learn about online. The owner never builds anything, manages tokens or needs to know how to use AI.

plates.head: Ben Palaskas, founder.
lines: Built AMTECH alone, from the first line of code in late August: the platform, the agent swarm, the self-serve sign-up and the website.
Sold AMTECH's first customers himself, before there was a public product.
AMTECH is built the way it runs: one founder directing a swarm of agents. The company is its own first proof.
With the raise: a founding engineer, a go-to-market engineer and a marketer.

plates.head: $2M seed.
lines: To ten thousand businesses in 18 months.
Three hires: A founding engineer, a go-to-market engineer and a marketer.
New industries: A new product for a new industry every few weeks.
In 18 months: 10,000 paying businesses. About 100 of them across several private equity firms, each paying AMTECH 8% of its revenue.
AMTECH's own businesses: The first businesses started and run by our own swarms.
